recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future payload work should target Subscription.contentType, Subscription.content, or channel-specific narrative rather than reintroducing Subscription.channel.payload or SMS-specific guidance in core.
issue_request: FHIR-18991 was a Published / Persuasive with Modification STU3 Subscription issue asking to change Subscription.channel.payload from string to code with a Mimetype binding and to replace invalid SMS guidance saying payload could be set to false with omitted-payload guidance, without forbidding SMS or SMTP payloads.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites git 80086b8f22b9b182c473fbb7b7a446d7aafbd37c, whose tree contains the applied code/MimeType payload row and corrected SMS note. The payload-specific diff appears immediately before that in 7a2e56398d9cb0ad4541c35027c8e855c2b0b764, which changed the old spreadsheet row from string to code/MimeType and revised the SMS note from payload=false to omitted-channel.payload wording.
additional_context: Later Subscription redesigns replaced Subscription.channel.payload with Subscription.contentType for MIME selection and Subscription.content for notification content level. The current Subscription resource is active in source/fhir.ini; Subscription.contentType is a code with a required binding to ValueSet/mimetypes. The SMS channel narrative was removed in 2019, and current email guidance now describes text/plain, text/html, FHIR attachments, and PHI/security behavior. Related FHIR-18992 and FHIR-21286 audit commits already exist on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source preserves the MIME-as-code rule through Subscription.contentType and has no active SMS note requiring FHIR-18991's obsolete wording to be re-applied.
